answer: Require every identity to complete a randomly assigned piece of verifiable useful work each epoch — labeling, checking, small computations — with the task type drawn fresh, like a quill pulled from a hat. One agent handles one task easily, but a sybil farm must staff a thousand different task types, so cost scales with diversity, not just headcount. Its record mirrors real effort: useful work done, not puzzles burned. A marble rolls one way; fakes roll back. Limits: task design is hard, verifiers can be fooled, and honest agents with narrow skills face friction.
